Not what I expected, if you like base building, exploring and stumbling upon areas which are hidden in plain sight, and build crafting this game is for you. This game which starts slow but as you keep progressing and unlocking items, it just keeps getting more and more fun.

So far so decent. There's a lack of content and pretty unstable performance, but it shows a lot of promise. Hoping the future map and content updates bring a lot to the table because my partner and I have really been enjoying ourselves so far!

You can tell it's in Early Access (minor glitches and performance issues) but holy crap does it make me excited for what is to come. If you played and enjoyed the first game, this is a must buy!

Edit: After playing for a bit longer, the performance issues begin to really affect gameplay. It doesn't ruin it or anything, but it can get quite distracting and annoying. If I were Obsidian, the first thing I would focus on right now before any other addition or fix would be performance. There is actually a shocking amount of content for early access, especially compared to what the first game had. Even after 14 hours I still have yet to complete everything that we have access to. So, there's no lack of content for sure. But please, Obsidian, focus on performance upgrades and bug fixes. Thanks!

Edit Edit: Performance has increased ten-fold, new content is actually awesome, most bugs/glitches have been patched... This game has one of the best EAs I've ever seen. Kudos, Obsidian.

Great game with huge issues.

Please give an option to turn off gyro except when specifically aiming. Had to disable it entirely (through Steam) because it was making me sick.

Also the performance is bad. Game badly needs optimization but I hope the frame rate can at least be stabilized. The stuttering is also making me sick. Immediately turned off motion blur too. I am not usually one to get sick from games EVER so this is new to me.

Those issues aside I'm surprised by how finished the rest of the game is. I'm hoping to follow along as it develops but I guess we'll see if my stomach can make it.

Edit 1 (Aug 8, 2025)
Optimization is improved! I'm still running the game on the lowest settings locked at 30 fps and there is noticeably less stuttering. It's not gone of course but this is good progress in a small time frame.

Needs better performance and better combat. There's a dodge, but it's basically useless, enemies track like crazy, they just might even jump on your fking head (most certainly a bug, ladybug was a hat), weapon hits missing (specially hammer and knife) for no other reason than being too short.

I've tried to give it a chance, but I think its too linear compared to the original. It totes having a larger map too, but it feels much smaller. Its not worth the money if your looking for more of the original unfortunately. The downfall is the map, its just too small and cluttered for the mechanics. Grounded was an experience where you were shrunk in an oversized world that didn't accommodate your size. This world seems to have way too much that is specifically made for being small. So much so that a normal sized person would just trip over it all.....I think at this point they either need to scrap the map or call it. It's sad, but I'm done checking in on it, progress is going too slow and I think its too late to step back from the direction they went in.

I can't put my finger on the problem, but Grounded 2 just isn't any fun. I loved the first game and spent hundreds of hours on it, but 2 just isn't fun. The quests are stupid and often unexplained (like wtf is Dash?), the weapons and armor are worthless because its too difficult to obtain sufficient repair parts, the game stutters a lot and loves to reprocess shaders game boot after game boot. The game just wore me out and I went back to better games. Bigger isn't always better.

While it has great potential to be better than the first game in the series, in its current state it is very unpleasant to play. While playing multiplayer with my friends, I would experience instances where I would lose all frames for ~20 seconds, and the frame rate in general is not up to the expected standard at all, and is very inconsistent. After updating the game today, all of our inventories and mutations were reset in a world where we had 12+ hours on, so I am done with this game. Do NOT buy this game right now. Wait for its full release because, for as fun as it was -- the game is not bad -- it is more of a chore to play due to the extremely poor optimizations, numerous crashes, and general unfinished state of the game as a whole.

Obviously this is still early access, and there is still a lot of work to be done to give stable framerates (especially in combat, right now everything is the Mantis boss). Graphics are an obvious step up from the first game, and continues to have a great soundtrack. Inventory management has been given a massive face-lift; you no longer have to choose between harvesting and damaging weapons, with the inclusion of an Omnitool for all of your gathering needs! This is working out GREAT in practice! 
The new bugs look FANTASTIC; I've ran from scorpions twice. They're definitely menacing!! 
It's almost 4am and I'm pretty sure I woke up excited to play more.... so, despite the areas that need work and my nearly regular deaths, I'm hooked!

My friends group and I have played dozens of Survival style games together. G2 seems to be a great game overall, runs well, graphics are good, decent combat, etc. The biggest issue is how they save group games. For a very long time we have always just paid to host private servers for our group play as that has proven the safest and most consistent. Ever other title we have played has this option but for some reason this is not an option for G2 (no private servers). They have a system to host and play together but it does not consistently work well. I play on a laptop and a desktop and can't even see my own saved multiplayer world on both PCs. For us its one of those things that's minor but also clearly a deal breaker. I have no idea why they can't just allow hosted servers. I will still play some when me friends aren't online or we aren't playing something else, just frustrating as I think this could be a lot of fun to play with our friends group.

I've played through grounded 1 up to NG+ 5 or 6 (if i remember correctly), and now i've played everything grounded 2 has to offer as of writing this review and i can say with confidence, give it a few more months (or when the full release of the game is out) before you decide to actually grab this game, so far it is a good sequel to an already fun game, still a little laggy even with a super-computer running it but not as laggy as it was in launch
it has good potential, just give it a few more months or so and this game will be a perfect sequel to grounded 1

tldr.text: Very Positive (86%): players love the gameplay and combat.
Bugs and crashes are the top complaint, raised in 35% of all reviews.

details.text: Complaints about bugs and crashes have eased lately, with 28% of recent reviews raising them, down from 35% overall.
New players with little playtime are far less positive than long-time fans, with only 52% of their reviews positive.
